title: Foot exam in diabetes (sensation check)
what: The doctor examines your feet and checks how well they feel touch, vibration, and temperature. This helps avoid missing foot sores.
why: For everyone with diabetes, usually once a year, and more often if there are foot problems.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes, with the conclusion right away
tell_doctor: Whether you have numbness, burning, or tingling in your legs
Calluses, cracks, or sores that heal slowly

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Come in your usual shoes and socks, as the doctor will look at them too.

prepare.title: Feet
prepare.text: Do not trim your nails too short the day before, and do not cut calluses yourself.

prepare.title: Sugar
prepare.text: Bring your sugar records or HbA1c test results.

bring: A sugar diary and recent tests
steps: You take off your shoes and socks
The doctor examines the skin, nails, and the spaces between your toes
Touches your feet with a thin nylon filament, and you say where you feel it
Places a tuning fork to check vibration
Checks the pulse in your feet
Explains how to care for your feet
feel: The touches are light, sometimes ticklish
after: Check your feet at home every day, with a mirror if you like
Wear comfortable shoes that do not rub
The follow-up exam is after the time your doctor sets
red_flags: A sore, ulcer, or redness on the foot that does not go away: see a doctor urgently
The foot turned black, is very swollen, or is hot to the touch: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Why check my feet if nothing hurts?
faq.a: With diabetes, feeling goes down without you noticing. You may not feel a sore.
Better not to. A foot care specialist does it.

reminders.text: Foot exam tomorrow. Come in your usual shoes and bring your sugar diary.
